context: Staging has been allocated capacity for four concurrent tasks; supported worker concurrency is an integer from one to eight. Change the staging setting from two to four and update the deployment guide to agree. Keep the local HTTP binding, queue bound, retry schedule, and payload logging settings. Documentation and configuration are reviewable even without a structural graph adapter.

base.deploy/staging.toml:
[service]
name = "dispatch-worker"
environment = "staging"
region = "local"
log_level = "info"

[worker]
concurrency = 2
maximum_pending = 128
retry_delays_seconds = [1, 3, 9]
timeout_seconds = 45
drain_seconds = 60

[http]
bind_host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 8095
health_path = "/health"

[logging]
include_payloads = false
format = "json"
base.README.md:
# Dispatch worker staging deployment

The staging instance runs the dispatch worker on the same host as its proxy.
It listens only on the loopback interface and exposes a local health route.
Application payloads are excluded from service logs.

## Worker capacity

The staging worker uses **2 concurrent tasks**.
The pending queue permits 128 tasks before admission pauses.
Retry delays are 1, 3, and 9 seconds.
A task has a 45-second execution deadline.
Deployment shutdown allows 60 seconds for draining active tasks.

## Health and logs

The health endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:8095/health`.
Health success reports process liveness, not downstream delivery success.
Logs use the JSON format at the info level.
Payload logging remains disabled in staging.
